title: Tensor product of a separably generated field extension with a reduced algebra is reduced
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S$ be a reduced $k$-algebra (a commutative $k$-algebra with no nonzero nilpotent elements), and let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is separably generated over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1): there is a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $K/k$ such that $K/k(x_i;i\in I)$ is separable algebraic. Then the ring $K\otimes_kS$ (the tensor product of the $k$-algebras $K$ and $S$, with multiplication $(a\otimes s)(a'\otimes s')=aa'\otimes ss'$ and unit $1\otimes1$) is reduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, line 10152), the case 'K/k separably generated' (second paragraph of its proof, which reduces to the finitely generated separably generated case treated in the first paragraph); the case 'K/k separable' of 030U is not part of this node

proof.text: (Reduction to finitely generated pieces.) Let $z\in K\otimes_kS$ with $z^m=0$ for some $m\ge1$; we show $z=0$. Write $z=\sum_{j=1}^na_j\otimes s_j$ with $a_j\in K$, $s_j\in S$. Fix a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] with $K$ separable algebraic over $k(x_i;i\in I)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-separating-transcendence-basis-finite-subextension] applied to $a_1,\dots,a_n$ there is a finite $T\subseteq I$ such that, with $L=k(x_i;i\in T)$ and $K'=L(a_1,\dots,a_n)\subseteq K$, the extension $K'/L$ is finite and separable algebraic; the family $(x_i)_{i\in T}$ is algebraically independent over $k$, being a subfamily of an algebraically independent family. Let $S'\subseteq S$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by $s_1,\dots,s_n$: it is of finite type over $k$, and reduced since it is a subring of the reduced ring $S$. Every $k$-module is flat over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so by the definition of flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] tensoring the injective $k$-linear map $K'\to K$ with $S'$, and the injective $k$-linear map $S'\to S$ with $K$, gives injective maps $K'\otimes_kS'\to K\otimes_kS'\to K\otimes_kS$. Their composite is the ring homomorphism $a\otimes s\mapsto a\otimes s$, which maps $z'=\sum_ja_j\otimes s_j\in K'\otimes_kS'$ to $z$; it maps $z'^m$ to $z^m=0$, so $z'^m=0$ by injectivity, and $z=0$ follows once $z'=0$. Hence it suffices to prove: $K'\otimes_kS'$ is reduced whenever $S'$ is a reduced $k$-algebra of finite type and $K'$ is a finite separable algebraic extension of $L=k(x_i;i\in T)$ with $T$ finite and $(x_i)_{i\in T}$ algebraically independent over $k$.

proof.text: (Reduction to a field in place of $S'$.) The field $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so the finite type $k$-algebra $S'$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Let $\mathfrak q_1,\dots,\mathfrak q_t$ be its minimal primes and $W\subseteq S'$ its set of nonzerodivisors. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] the total ring of fractions $W^{-1}S'$ is isomorphic, as an $S'$-algebra, to $F_1\times\cdots\times F_t$ with $F_l=S'_{\mathfrak q_l}$ a field. The map $S'\to W^{-1}S'$ is injective: $s/1=0$ means $ws=0$ for some $w\in W$, hence $s=0$ as $w$ is a nonzerodivisor. So there is an injective $k$-algebra map $S'\to F_1\times\cdots\times F_t$, and each $F_l$ is a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] through $k\to S'\to F_l$. Since $K'$ is flat over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the ring map $K'\otimes_kS'\to K'\otimes_k(F_1\times\cdots\times F_t)$ is injective, and by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] (with the two factors of the tensor product exchanged) the map $a\otimes(f_l)_l\mapsto(a\otimes f_l)_l$ is a bijection $K'\otimes_k(F_1\times\cdots\times F_t)\to\prod_{l=1}^tK'\otimes_kF_l$; it is a ring homomorphism, as one checks on pure tensors. A product of finitely many reduced rings is reduced (componentwise), and a subring of a reduced ring is reduced. So $K'\otimes_kS'$ is reduced once $K'\otimes_kF$ is reduced for every field extension $F/k$ (for $t=0$, i.e. $S'=0$, there is nothing to prove).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U, lines 10165-10169 ('S embeds into a finite product of fields, namely its total ring of fractions', citing Lemmas Tag 00EU lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring and Tag 02LX lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points); Stacks then reduces to a domain, here to each field factor

proof.text: ($L\otimes_kF$ is a domain.) Let $F/k$ be a field extension, $T=\{t_1,\dots,t_r\}$ and $P=k[X_1,\dots,X_r]$ the polynomial ring, an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. Since $x_{t_1},\dots,x_{t_r}$ are algebraically independent over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], the $k$-algebra map $P\to L$, $X_j\mapsto x_{t_j}$, is injective; its image $k[x_{t_1},\dots,x_{t_r}]$ together with all quotients $u/v$ ($v\ne0$) of its elements is a subfield of $L$ containing $k$ and the $x_{t_j}$, hence all of $L$; so $L$ is the field of fractions of $P$. Let $C=F\otimes_kP$; by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=k$, $R=F$) $C\cong F[X_1,\dots,X_r]$, $c\otimes f\mapsto c\bar f$, an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain]. The map $P\to C$, $f\mapsto1\otimes f$, sends $f$ to $f$ with its coefficients read in $F$ through the injective map $k\to F$, so a nonzero $f$ has nonzero image. By [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] (with $A=P$, $K=L$ and this $C$) the ring $L\otimes_PC$ is an integral domain. By associativity of tensor products, $L\otimes_PC=L\otimes_P(P\otimes_kF)\cong(L\otimes_PP)\otimes_kF\cong L\otimes_kF$ as rings ($\lambda\otimes(f\otimes c)\mapsto\lambda f\otimes c$). Hence $A:=L\otimes_kF$ is an integral domain; let $E$ be its field of fractions. The composite $L\to A\to E$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, is a homomorphism of fields, so $E$ is a field extension of $L$ [def-pc-field-extension], and $A\to E$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U, lines 10174-10177 ('It is easy to see that k[x_1,...,x_r] ⊗_k S = S[x_1,...,x_r] is a domain. This implies k(x_1,...,x_r) ⊗_k S is a domain as it is a localization of S[x_1,...,x_r]'), with S = F

proof.text: (Conclusion.) With $F$, $A=L\otimes_kF$ and $E$ as in step 3, the map $a\otimes c\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes c)$ is a ring isomorphism $K'\otimes_kF\cong K'\otimes_L(L\otimes_kF)=K'\otimes_LA$ (associativity of tensor products, $K'$ an $L$-algebra). As $K'$ is a flat $L$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the injection $A\to E$ gives an injective ring homomorphism $K'\otimes_LA\to K'\otimes_LE$. Since $K'/L$ is finite and separable algebraic (step 1) and $E/L$ is a field extension (step 3), $K'\otimes_LE$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced]. A subring of a reduced ring is reduced, so $K'\otimes_kF$ is reduced for every field extension $F/k$. By step 2, $K'\otimes_kS'$ is reduced, and by step 1, $K\otimes_kS$ is reduced.
